physical_plan_observation.scan: Spark 4.2.0 FileScan parquet for all four reads; projection read only source_system, typed ID, id, and lookup_hash.
physical_plan_observation.id_pushdown: Not verified: Spark's rendered PushedFilters text is truncated after the type filter. The submitted SQL predicate includes the exact id equality.
physical_plan_observation.limitation: Plans show observed hash/source/type filters pushed into a Parquet scan; the full exact ID predicate is present in SQL but its pushdown is not visible in the truncated plan. No file-pruning counters or executed clustering proof were captured; this is not evidence of file pruning.

napkin_arithmetic_only.basis_and_limits: For this fixture, hash chunks are about 8.0 compressed bytes per row at both scales, as expected for high-entropy signed BIGINT hashes; aggregate active bytes settle near 11.3 bytes/row. The same four output files per table at both scales make fixed per-file structures and compression of repetitive fields a larger share of the small sample, so bytes per row fall as those costs are amortized. This supports near-linear bytes for the synthetic fixed-width/highly repetitive fixture, not realistic property or source history. Arithmetic is not a capacity or total-publication forecast.

scope_limits: No full-table count/distinct/collision search was run; Parquet footer row counts confirmed the written row counts.

Historical local[4] 1B/5B write estimates were 45.47 minutes (two-point affine) and 56.73 minutes (10M/50M average-rate basis); the later local[18] calibration projects 18.05 minutes at 80% measured throughput. Full run remains held for review; see the 18-core evidence packet.

four_core_historical_projection.status: Historical 4-core model; superseded by the later 18-core calibration for current throughput evidence.
four_core_historical_projection.basis: 4-core 10M/50M write rates; require 80% of those measured rates; writes only.

host_observation.note: Host capacity observation only; no throughput scaling to 18 cores is assumed or qualified.

four_core_historical_projection.exclusions: No setup or table-creation time, metadata growth, graph export/execution, publication, source history/retention, validation/retry, or real production payloads included. 4-core point forecast exceeds 15-minute review threshold; no full run approved.

two_point_affine_model_at_80_percent.assumptions: For each table, fit elapsed write seconds = intercept + slope × rows through the 1M/5M and 10M/50M write measurements; apply the same 0.8 throughput factor to the fitted duration. The fit yields about 45.47 minutes versus 56.73 minutes from applying 80% to the 10M/50M average write rates. Two points do not establish the scaling law; both estimates exceed the 15-minute review threshold, so the higher value remains the conservative planning basis.
